authored.note: Explanations are written for learners. Facts are checked word for word against the cited files. The evidence in Practice is read from the committed specimen packs, unedited.

summary.text: An external scanner flags a tool description. What can a SOC actually conclude? This lab lays the scanner's recorded findings next to the runtime's recorded decisions for the same descriptions, joined by the description's SHA-256, and asks what each kind of evidence can and cannot prove.
facts: when an external security scanner flags agent/tool metadata, what can the SOC actually conclude from that evidence?

glance.label: The scenario
glance.text: A static scanner examined two catalog snapshots, one normal and one with a manipulative description. The agent runtime separately recorded the same descriptions and its decisions.

glance.label: Three evidence planes
glance.text: Scanner evidence, runtime metadata evidence, and authorization and execution evidence. Each proves something different.
facts: Name the three evidence planes and what each can prove.

glance.label: How the planes are joined
glance.text: By the description's SHA-256, not by the whole artifact's hash.
facts: Correlate scanner and runtime evidence with description SHA-256, not artifact.sha256.

glance.label: What a scanner finding is not
glance.text: It is not an authorization decision, and zero findings is not proof of safety.

glance.label: Why the attack ran and the retest did not
glance.text: The attack ran because of the vulnerable profile. The retest did not because the tool control denied it and the handler never began.
facts: Explain ATTACK execution as the vulnerable profile, not scanner HIGH.
Explain RETEST non-execution as CTRL-MCP-001 DENY plus runtime handler count 0.

scenarios.label: RETEST: same manipulative description, defended profile

questions.prompt: Does the description hash the runtime recorded for the ATTACK run equal the hash the scanner recorded for the MALICIOUS scan?

quote.text: Correlate scanner and runtime evidence with description SHA-256, not artifact.sha256.

questions.teach: The join key is the description hash that both planes recorded.

questions.prompt: Does the runtime's BASELINE description hash equal the hash on the NORMAL scan?

quote.text: Correlate scanner and runtime evidence with description SHA-256, not artifact.sha256.

questions.teach: Same join, on the normal description.

questions.prompt: How many findings did the scanner record for the NORMAL scan?
questions.teach: Zero findings means the scan ran and found nothing, not that the tool is safe.

questions.prompt: The ATTACK and RETEST runs carry the same description hash. Is the hash the same?

quote.text: Show ATTACK and RETEST used the same malicious description hash.

questions.teach: Same hash, so the description alone cannot explain a different outcome.

questions.prompt: What did CTRL-MCP-001 decide about the follow-on request in the RETEST run?
questions.teach: The decision comes from the authorization control, not from the scanner.

questions.prompt: Did the follow-on handler for lookup_customer_tier begin in the ATTACK run?

quote.text: Explain ATTACK execution as the vulnerable profile, not scanner HIGH.

questions.teach: Execution started under the vulnerable profile; the scanner's HIGH did not cause or prevent it.
